Laws of Sacrifice

precepts.text: This is how you esteemed the day. On the sabbath day, two lambs of the first year without spot, with the meat offering of flour mingled with oil and the drink offering thereof: this is the burnt offering of every sabbath. In the beginnings of your months, the new moon: two young bullocks, one ram, seven lambs of the first year without spot, with their meat offerings and drink offerings measured out in hins of wine, and one kid of the goats for a sin offering. This is what the Pharisees were judging the people on.
precepts.point: Let no man therefore judge you in meat, or in drink, or in respect of an holy day, or of the new moon, or of the sabbath days. The meat is the meat offerings and the drink is the drink offerings; do not let a Christian use this verse to say it is talking about eating pork or getting drunk. This is why Paul said bring the books and the parchments: everything he wrote was based on what the scriptures said.

note.label: Deceived by Enticing Words: Colossians 2

precepts.why:
This is how you esteemed the day, and this is what the Pharisees were judging the people on. “And on the sabbath day two lambs of the first year without spot, and two tenth deals of flour for a meat offering, mingled with oil, and the drink offering thereof:” “This is the burnt offering of every sabbath”. Two lambs that are one year old: that is how you esteemed the sabbath.

Now watch the new moon: “in the beginnings of your months ye shall offer a burnt offering unto the Lord; two young bullocks, and one ram, seven lambs of the first year without spot”. Two young bulls, one ram and seven lambs on a new moon, one year old, without blemish. The meat offering was flour “mingled with oil”, measured for each bullock, each ram and each lamb, “for a burnt offering of a sweet savour, a sacrifice made by fire unto the Lord.”

“And their drink offerings shall be half an hin of wine unto a bullock, and the third part of an hin unto a ram, and a fourth part of an hin unto a lamb”. There was a measuring instrument you had to use to measure the wine; the drink offerings were men pouring out wine. “this is the burnt offering of every month throughout the months of the year.” “And one kid of the goats for a sin offering”.

So “Let no man therefore judge you in meat, or in drink, or in respect of an holyday, or of the new moon, or of the sabbath days” is meat offerings and drink offerings: on certain high holy days so many lambs or goats, on the new moon the bullocks, ram and seven lambs, on the sabbath the meat and drink offerings. Do not let a Christian use that verse to say it is talking about pork and getting drunk. That is why Paul said bring the books and the parchments: everything he wrote was based on what the scriptures said. And they “are a shadow of things to come; but the body is of Christ.”

precepts.text: The priests in the temple profane the sabbath, and are blameless; the sabbath offerings were commanded work.
precepts.point: This is also why Christ had to come. In captivity we have no lambs, no farms, no temple, no most holy place, no veil, no high priest; the handwriting of ordinances that was against us was taken out of the way and nailed to his cross. Those who deny Christ and claim the Old Testament only are not keeping these sacrifices, and without Christ the whole law, drink offering to meat offering, still stands over them.

note.label: Numbers 28: The Continual Burnt Offering and the Offerings of the Feasts

precepts.why:
On the sabbath day two more lambs were offered with their meat and drink offerings, “the burnt offering of every sabbath, beside the continual burnt offering”: four lambs every sabbath, with the drink offerings attached. Precept upon precept this answers what Christ told the Pharisees.

“Or have ye not read in the law, how that on the sabbath days the priests in the temple profane the sabbath, and are blameless?” Israel did not kindle fire for themselves on the sabbath, but this altar work was the ordinance of the Lord for every sabbath day. The priests were commanded to do it, so they were blameless.

precepts.text: The handwriting of ordinances against us was nailed to the cross; let no man judge you in meat, or in drink, or of an holyday, or of the new moon, or of the sabbath days, which are a shadow of things to come, but the body is of Christ.
precepts.point: This is also why Christ had to come. In captivity we have no lambs, no farms, no temple, no most holy place, no veil, no high priest; the handwriting of ordinances that was against us was taken out of the way and nailed to his cross. Those who deny Christ and claim the Old Testament only are not keeping these sacrifices, and without Christ the whole law, drink offering to meat offering, still stands over them.

note.label: Numbers 28: The Continual Burnt Offering and the Offerings of the Feasts

precepts.why:
The burnt offering of every sabbath is also why Christ had to come. In captivity we have no lambs, no farms, no temple, no most holy place, no veil, no high priest. “Blotting out the handwriting of ordinances that was against us, which was contrary to us, and took it out of the way, nailing it to his cross.”

“Let no man therefore judge you in meat, or in drink, or in respect of an holyday, or of the new moon, or of the sabbath days: Which are a shadow of things to come; but the body is of Christ.” The meat and drink offerings of the sabbath were a shadow of things to come, and the body is of Christ.

Those who deny Christ and claim the Old Testament only are not keeping these sacrifices, and without Christ the whole law, drink offering to meat offering, still stands over them.

precepts.text: He taketh away the first covenant of sacrifices to establish the second; we are sanctified through the offering of the body of Jesus Christ once for all, while the priests stood daily offering sacrifices which can never take away sins.
precepts.point: He taketh away the first, that he may establish the second: Christ offered his body once for all, where the priests stood daily offering the same sacrifices which can never take away sins. Thank the Most High for Jesus Christ, because these ordinances cannot be fulfilled in captivity.

note.label: Numbers 28: The Continual Burnt Offering and the Offerings of the Feasts

precepts.why:
The day of the firstfruits carried two young bullocks, one ram, seven lambs, their meat and drink offerings, and a kid of the goats to make an atonement, beside the continual burnt offering. Every feast carried offerings stacked upon the daily offering, and missing them was sin.

“Above when he said, Sacrifice and offering and burnt offerings and offering for sin thou wouldest not, neither hadst pleasure therein; which are offered by the law; Then said he, Lo, I come to do thy will, O God. He taketh away the first, that he may establish the second.” The Lord said by David that He would not have the sacrifices; they could never make the comers thereunto perfect, for the people went right back to their sin.

“By the which will we are sanctified through the offering of the body of Jesus Christ once for all. And every priest standeth daily ministering and offering oftentimes the same sacrifices, which can never take away sins.” Christ offered his body once for all, where the priests stood daily offering the same sacrifices which can never take away sins.

Thank the Most High for Jesus Christ, because these ordinances cannot be fulfilled in captivity.

precepts.text: The burnt offering of every sabbath: the priests sacrificed a lamb in the morning and in the evening on the sabbath because the Lord commanded it.
precepts.point: Christ spoke about that fire in the temple: on the sabbath days the priests in the temple profane the sabbath, and are blameless. Israel was not to kindle a fire on the sabbath when it comes to food, but the priests had to keep that fire burning, and they sacrificed on the sabbath days, a lamb in the morning and a lamb in the evening; they broke the sabbath yet are blameless, because they were doing thus saith the Lord.

note.label: 1 Samuel 3: The Lord Reveals Himself to Samuel

precepts.why:
“And on the sabbath day two lambs of the first year without spot”: “This is the burnt offering of every sabbath, beside the continual burnt offering, and his drink offering.” The priests sacrificed a lamb in the morning and a lamb in the evening on the sabbath, because the Lord commanded it.

That is how the priests in the temple could “profane the sabbath” and be “blameless”: the fire was kept burning and the offering made on the sabbath because it was thus saith the Lord.

precepts.text: Two lambs of the first year without spot were offered day by day for a continual burnt offering.
precepts.point: Solomon confessed that the house he built was great, for great is our God above all gods, yet the heaven and heaven of heavens cannot contain Him. He asked Huram for a cunning man to work in gold, silver, brass, iron, and colored cloth, and for cedar, fir, and algum trees out of Lebanon, promising wheat, barley, wine, and oil to the hewers.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 2: Solomon Prepares to Build the House

precepts.why:
“This is the offering made by fire which ye shall offer unto the Lord; two lambs of the first year without spot day by day, for a continual burnt offering.”

The daily offering was two lambs, one in the morning and one in the evening. That is what Solomon named: “the burnt offerings morning and evening.” “This is an ordinance for ever to Israel.”

precepts.text: On the sabbath day two lambs of the first year were offered, beside the continual burnt offering.
precepts.point: Solomon confessed that the house he built was great, for great is our God above all gods, yet the heaven and heaven of heavens cannot contain Him. He asked Huram for a cunning man to work in gold, silver, brass, iron, and colored cloth, and for cedar, fir, and algum trees out of Lebanon, promising wheat, barley, wine, and oil to the hewers.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 2: Solomon Prepares to Build the House

precepts.why:
“And on the sabbath day two lambs of the first year without spot, and two tenth deals of flour for a meat offering, mingled with oil, and the drink offering thereof.”

The sabbath offering added two more lambs beside the continual burnt offering. Solomon built the house for the burnt offerings “on the sabbaths” as well, and “This is an ordinance for ever to Israel.”

precepts.text: In the beginning of their months Israel offered a burnt offering unto the Lord, which is the new moon.
precepts.point: Solomon confessed that the house he built was great, for great is our God above all gods, yet the heaven and heaven of heavens cannot contain Him. He asked Huram for a cunning man to work in gold, silver, brass, iron, and colored cloth, and for cedar, fir, and algum trees out of Lebanon, promising wheat, barley, wine, and oil to the hewers.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 2: Solomon Prepares to Build the House

precepts.why:
“And in the beginnings of your months ye shall offer a burnt offering unto the Lord; two young bullocks, and one ram, seven lambs of the first year without spot.”

The beginning of the months is the new moon, and it had its own burnt offering. Solomon named it with the rest: “on the sabbaths, and on the new moons, and on the solemn feasts of the Lord our God. This is an ordinance for ever to Israel.” That is why we keep them in the land of our captivity, according to the law given through Moses in the book of Numbers.

precepts.text: In the fourteenth day of the first month is the passover of the Lord.
precepts.point: Solomon confessed that the house he built was great, for great is our God above all gods, yet the heaven and heaven of heavens cannot contain Him. note.label: 2 Chronicles 2: Solomon Prepares to Build the House

precepts.why:
“And in the fourteenth day of the first month is the passover of the Lord.”

After the daily, sabbath and new moon offerings come the solemn feasts, beginning with the passover on the fourteenth day of the first month, and the feast of unleavened bread beginning the fifteenth day. These are “the solemn feasts of the Lord our God” Solomon built the house for, and “This is an ordinance for ever to Israel.”

precepts.text: The one lamb offered in the morning and the other at evening set the pattern of the daily sacrifice.
precepts.point: They burn the daily burnt sacrifices morning and evening, set the shewbread in order, and keep the charge of the Most High that Jeroboam forsook.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 13: Abijah Stands on the Covenant

precepts.why:
“The one lamb shalt thou offer in the morning, and the other lamb shalt thou offer at even.”

That is the pattern of the daily sacrifice, and Judah kept it: “they burn unto the Lord every morning and every evening burnt sacrifices and sweet incense.” They set the shewbread in order and lit the golden candlestick every evening. “for we keep the charge of the Lord our God; but ye have forsaken him.”

points: The Lord commanded the offerings made by fire to be observed in their due season: two lambs of the first year without spot, day by day, one lamb in the morning and the other lamb at even, a continual burnt offering which was ordained in mount Sinai.

note.label: Numbers 28: The Continual Burnt Offering and the Offerings of the Feasts

points: In the beginnings of your months, the new moon, a burnt offering was made: two young bullocks, one ram, seven lambs of the first year without spot, with their meat offerings of flour mingled with oil and their drink offerings of wine.

note.label: Numbers 28: The Continual Burnt Offering and the Offerings of the Feasts

points: A kid of the goats for a sin offering was added, and all of it was beside the continual burnt offering. This was the burnt offering of every month throughout the months of the year.

note.label: Numbers 28: The Continual Burnt Offering and the Offerings of the Feasts

points: The fourteenth day of the first month is the passover of the Lord, and the fifteenth day is the feast: seven days unleavened bread, bread without leaven, must be eaten.

note.label: Numbers 28: The Continual Burnt Offering and the Offerings of the Feasts

points: The first day and the seventh day are holy convocations wherein no manner of servile work is done, and each of the seven days carried its own sacrifice by fire: two young bullocks, a ram, seven lambs without blemish, with the meat offering of flour mingled with oil and a goat for a sin offering to make an atonement, beside the continual burnt offering of the morning.

That is on top of the passover lamb itself, which was not dressed like these offerings but roast with fire and eaten with the bitter herbs. Count the lambs of that week and you see how much the sacrifice law carried.

note.label: Numbers 28: The Continual Burnt Offering and the Offerings of the Feasts

points: The day of the firstfruits, the feast of weeks, when the new meat offering was brought after your weeks be out, was also an holy convocation with no servile work, with two young bullocks, one ram, seven lambs, their meat and drink offerings, and a kid of the goats to make an atonement, beside the continual burnt offering.
